rfm_tuples.R: Implied management commitment to capital allocation strategy following FY2025 results, ongoing restructuring program, and activist proxy contest (10-K filed 2026-02-19).
rfm_tuples.f: Parse all Form 4 XML filings 2024-11-01 through 2026-05-25 for code-P (open-market PURCHASES) and code-S (open-market SALES) by named executives and directors.
rfm_tuples.M_value: ONE open-market purchase in entire 12-month window: independent director David J. Henshall bought 10,000 sh @ $48.60 on 2025-08-08 for $486,000 (filed 2025-08-11). Against that, TWENTY code-S open-market sales totaling $5,974,278: Morgan-Prager (Chief Legal Officer) $3.04M Nov 2024 @ $60.46-61.07; Woodhams (Chief Revenue Officer) $2.12M Dec 2024-May 2025 @ $49.67-64.78; Unterman (director) $450K across May-Oct 2025 @ $55-56.70 (clearly a 10b5-1 plan, 7 evenly-spaced 910-share sells); Stalick (CAO) $115K spread out; Hughes (director) $49.5K @ $30.25 on 2026-05-21 (FOUR DAYS BEFORE CUTOFF, scaling OUT of weakness); Yamamoto (director) $200K Nov 2024 @ $62. CEO Owen Ryan, founder Therese Tucker (co-CEO), and CFO Patrick Villanova have ZERO code-P purchases AND ZERO code-S sales — all transactions are F (tax withholding), M (option exercise), A (grants), or G (gifts). P:S ratio = 0.081x — sells 12.3x bigger than the lone buy.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: After a -50.9% drawdown, with three restructuring rounds in 2025, two activist filers (Engaged Capital + Fivespan 5.1% 13D), and a 'rejected acquisition offer' headline, exactly ONE insider — a director, not the CEO/CFO/founder — has put $486K of personal capital into the stock. No C-suite conviction buying whatsoever. The Hughes sell on 2026-05-21 (T-4 to cutoff) into single-digit-volume liquidity is the opposite of the ABG-style 'CEO buys into the drawdown' signal that anchors the LONG-tier. Form 4 evidence directly REJECTS any management-conviction narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: the Henshall purchase represents informed insider conviction at a discounted price.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference Henshall's transaction date against the 8-K calendar (capital events, earnings, restructuring), and assess size relative to ownership.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Henshall joined BL board on 2025-04-02 (received initial RSU grant of 3,776 sh code-A on 2025-05-08). His purchase 2025-08-08 came 2 days AFTER Q2'25 10-Q (filed 2025-08-06) and Q2 earnings 8-K (2025-08-05) — i.e., outside the informational asymmetry window. Purchase size $486K vs $16,378 shares post-transaction = single-bet entry, not part of a scaling-in program. Henshall is a former CEO of Citrix and finance industry vet (clearly added to the board as a recovery-oriented director). Reduced his post-purchase holding 6,378 sh + 10,000 = 16,378 sh — material relative to his other holdings. Henshall received second annual RSU grant 6,416 sh on 2026-05-07 (code A, post-AGM) but did NOT add to position open-market post-drawdown despite the stock being ~38% lower ($30 vs $48.60). At the May 2026 AGM, Henshall received the LOWEST FOR/HIGHEST WITHHELD vote of three Class I directors (39.1M for / 9.5M withheld vs Davidson 44.6M/4.0M and Tucker 42.8M/5.8M) — signals investor concern about him specifically.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Henshall buy is the ONLY honest-insider data point but is partially undermined by (a) he is a brand-new director (newly aligned, not legacy management), (b) he did NOT add to position 9 months later at $30 when conviction would have been highest, (c) shareholders withheld 19.5% of votes vs him at AGM. This is a single positive data point in an otherwise selling tape — not enough to flip the verdict.

rfm_tuples.R: "We generated net income attributable to BlackLine, Inc. of $24.5 million, $161.2 million, and $52.8 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify magnitude and source of net income decline; reconcile reported GAAP NI vs core operating earnings (back out one-time items).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 7 results of operations + non-GAAP reconciliation)
rfm_tuples.M_value: GAAP NI collapsed 85% YoY: FY25 $24.5M vs FY24 $161.2M. The FY24 figure was INFLATED by a $65.1M gain on extinguishment of convertible senior notes (May 2024 partial repurchase of 2026 Notes) AND an $89.1M U.S. valuation allowance release ($43.1M tax benefit). FY25 underlying operating income $25.6M vs FY24 underlying operating income $18.5M is actually +38% on operations. But FY25 tax went from $43.1M benefit to $21.0M expense — a ~$64M swing on a $25M operating-income base. Diluted EPS $0.39 vs $1.45 (-73%). Non-GAAP EPS was $2.13 vs $2.18 — basically flat. So the GAAP collapse is a tax/extinguishment-gain reversal optical, NOT a true operating collapse.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically honest — the non-GAAP reconciliation makes the tax/extinguishment effects visible. But the GAAP headline is the story the market priced. The reported -85% NI compression coupled with already-decelerating revenue growth (7%) is what is driving the multiple compression activist Engaged Capital references.

rfm_tuples.R: "At December 31, 2025, we had 4,394 customers... For the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, no single customer accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues." Strategy framed as growth through new customer acquisition and platform pricing.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification) — given strategy is 'growth via new customers,' verify actual customer count trajectory across quarters.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K + Q1 2026 10-Q Key Metrics table — five trailing quarters)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Customer count trajectory: Q1'25=4,455, Q2'25=4,451, Q3'25=4,424, Q4'25=4,394, Q1'26=4,301. NET LOSS of 154 customers (-3.5%) over 5 quarters. Revenue grew 7% via price increases / platform-pricing model launched 2025. Dollar-based net retention rate wobbled: 104% → 105% → 103% → 105% → 105% (just barely above 100% means existing customers expanding only marginally faster than churn). 10-K dropped 'users' as a key metric in Q4'25 — disclosure gating that removes a comparable trend datapoint. WiseLayer acq (Dec 15, 2025, $23.6M total purchase price, including $16.75M goodwill / $4.0M intangibles on $0.0M acquired revenue) appears to be a 'narrative buy' of AI agents capability rather than a meaningful financial driver.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: customer-base shrinking while management narrative is centered on growth and new platform pricing. Existing customers are spending more, but the universe of paying customers is contracting — this is the classic mature-SaaS-with-churn signature. The dropped 'users' metric is a small but real disclosure-discipline regression.

rfm_tuples.R: "On March 4, 2025, we initiated a global restructuring program... During September 2025 and December 2025, we approved additional workforce reductions of 25 and 75 positions, respectively, including the planned closure of selected facilities."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify cadence and cumulative scope of workforce actions; assess whether single 'thoughtful' restructuring or escalating crisis-response.
rfm_tuples.M_value: THREE distinct restructuring approvals in calendar 2025: March 4 (130 positions / 7% of workforce), September 2025 (additional 25), December 2025 (additional 75 + facility closures). FY25 restructuring expense $14.6M vs FY24 $1.7M (+8.5x). Q1'26 additional $1.7M restructuring + $5.4M cash payments. Total positions cut ~230 across three rounds = ~12.4% of workforce. The Aug 2023 restructuring ($1.7M, 166 positions / 9%) makes this the SECOND major restructuring cycle in two years — i.e., the 2023 restructuring did NOT achieve sustainable cost discipline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Three escalating restructuring rounds in 9 months is a strong signal that management did NOT correctly size the right cost structure on the first cut. This is the operating pattern of a business in deteriorating end-demand (their own language: 'customers delay and defer purchasing decisions'). The frequency and ESCALATING size (130 → +25 → +75) suggests another round is plausible. Pattern matches Engaged Capital's 'inability to generate stockholder value' critique.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: Board governance is functioning and acting in stockholder interest. Filed DEFA14A and DEF14A reference 'cooperation agreement.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify whether the company faced a contested proxy and what the resolution was.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (DFAN14A filings by Engaged Capital + SC 13D by Fivespan Partners + DEF14A cooperation agreement)
rfm_tuples.M_value: TWO activists circling BL pre-cutoff: (1) Engaged Capital (Glenn Welling) filed DFAN14A 2026-01-13, 2026-01-20, 2026-01-27, 2026-02-02 — accused Board of 'outright rejection of a credible acquisition proposal without further engagement' and called the Board's plan to shrink the Board 'an entrenchment maneuver.' (2) Fivespan Partners (Dylan Haggart) filed SC 13D 2026-03-12 disclosing 5.1% / 3,013,943 share stake — i.e., second activist in addition to Engaged. Settlement: BL signed Cooperation Agreement 2026-03-09; Storm Duncan and Megan Prichard appointed to Board 2026-03-11 (two of Engaged's nominees). At 2026-05-07 AGM, the stockholder proposal to DECLASSIFY the Board PASSED overwhelmingly: 48.4M for vs 183K against. Say-on-pay was contested: 30.3M for vs 18.3M against (38% against). Owen Ryan signed an 'Employment Agreement Amendment' 2026-05-06 (immediately pre-AGM) — suggests retention package adjusted under activist pressure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K narrative does not mention the activist pressure or the alleged rejected acquisition proposal — though by the proxy season (March) the company disclosed it. Mode B catch: the issuer-controlled story is one of 'AI transformation' and 'platform pricing,' but the parallel story disclosed via DFAN14As / 13Ds is that institutional capital has lost confidence in independence as the value-maximizing path. 38% AGAINST on say-on-pay and ~20% withheld vs Henshall is uncommon investor revolt. M&A optionality is REAL upside, but the rejected-proposal precedent and entrenchment signals make a deal-now scenario uncertain.

rfm_tuples.R: "At December 31, 2025, we had $230.2 million aggregate principal amount of our 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due in 2026 (the '2026 Notes')... we plan to, and believe we are able to, make all expected principal and interest payments in the next 12 months."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify in Q1 2026 10-Q whether the $230.2M maturity was honored in cash and the resulting liquidity position.
rfm_tuples.M_value: VERIFIED: 'On March 15, 2026, the scheduled maturity date of the 0.00% 2026 Notes, the Company repaid the total outstanding $230.2 million aggregate principal amount pursuant to the terms of the 2026 Notes with cash on hand.' Balance sheet shows the current convertible senior notes liability went from $230.0M at 12/31/25 to $0 at 3/31/26. Cash + marketable securities dropped from $778.2M to $525.1M ($242M cash + $283M marketable). Remaining debt: $675M 1.00% 2029 Notes (initial conversion price $68.47, far out of money at $30 — won't convert before 2029). 2026 Capped Calls (strike $166.23 / cap $233.31) expired worthless. Liquidity adequate: $525M cash/MS vs $675M 2029 debt due 2029, OCF run-rate ~$170M/year.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure and execution: the 2026 maturity was retired cleanly in cash on the maturity date. This was the most concrete near-term default risk in the 10-K and management nailed it. The 2029 Notes are well-termed (1% coupon, 2029 maturity, conversion price $68 vs stock at $30). Balance sheet is not the source of the distress.

rfm_tuples.R: "We repurchased and retired approximately 4.5 million shares of common stock for $235.5 million during the year ended December 31, 2025" and "approximately 1.2 million shares of common stock for $47.1 million during the quarter ended March 31, 2026." Implied capital-allocation discipline at current valuations.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check buyback execution prices vs current price; compare CEO/CFO open-market activity vs company buyback timing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Item 5 issuer purchases + Note 11 Q1 stockholders equity)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY25 buyback: 4.5M sh for $235.5M = avg $52.33 vs current ~$30 (cutoff). Q1 2026 buyback: 1.2M sh for $47.1M = avg $39.25 vs current ~$30. Total $283M deployed at avg ~$50 — currently ~40% below execution price. Authorization expanded: from $200M to $400M on 2025-09-04 (Board), then $400M to $500M on 2026-03-13 (post-Engaged Capital settlement). $217.4M remaining authorization at 3/31/26. CEO Owen Ryan did NOT personally buy ANY shares open-market into this drawdown — i.e., the company is buying but the executives are not, which contrasts with the ABG pattern (where the CEO personally bought $1M at $204 within 2 weeks of his 10-K).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback discipline is poor — company deployed $283M at prices the stock then halved through. More importantly: the BUYBACK / PERSONAL-BUY DIVERGENCE is a soft red flag. When ABG's CEO personally bought $1M alongside the company's repurchase, that was conviction. At BL, the company-level buyback continues but no executive will deploy personal capital at $30-50 prices — i.e., management is willing to spend the SHAREHOLDERS' money but not their own.

rfm_tuples.R: BlackLine K.K. (Japan JV) deferred tax valuation allowance released in 2025; redeemable non-controlling interest carried at redemption value with $4,629K adjustment in Q1 2026.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — assess whether BlackLine K.K. NCI represents a hidden put-option liability and whether the YE25 valuation-allowance release was opportunistic.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K + Q1 2026 10-Q Note on income taxes and NCI)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Released BlackLine K.K. valuation allowance based on '3-year cumulative income position' — converted DTA into recognized asset just as BL is otherwise generating GAAP-NI compression. This adds ~$2.3M to net income beneficially. Redeemable NCI accounting: Q1 2026 adjustment of $4,629K vs $1,178K prior year — the NCI redemption value is moving materially. NCI structure means BL has minority partners in Japan with potential put rights that could require cash settlement; not quantified in current liabilities but indicates a non-disclosed cash demand if put exercised. WiseLayer acquisition recognized $16.75M goodwill on $245K AR + $19K PP&E acquired — i.e., goodwill = 71% of $23.6M purchase price for an early-stage AI capability.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch — the valuation allowance release is technically supported but timing is convenient (props GAAP NI in a year of operating deceleration). The NCI mark-to-market is a real but small balance-sheet pressure. WiseLayer goodwill-heavy structure is small enough to be immaterial but is the third 'narrative acquisition' in BL's history (FourQ, others) that builds goodwill on the balance sheet without commensurate revenue.

rfm_tuples.R: Stock-based compensation is part of 'investments in our people' (10-K compensation narrative). Non-GAAP measures back out SBC; capital structure relies on continued SBC issuance.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify SBC as % of revenue and net dilution pace; compare to buyback pace.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY25 SBC $96.3M on $700.4M revenue = 13.8% of revenue. Q1 2026 SBC $23.7M on $183.2M revenue = 12.9%. Annualized SBC run-rate $94.8M. RSU activity Q1 2026: vested 596K + 197K = 793K shares; new grants 81K + 146K = 227K. RSU pool at 3/31/26: 2,682K service-only + 146K + 90K perf + 396K market-conditioned = 3,314K unvested RSUs + 742K options outstanding. Outstanding shares ~58M => ~5.7% dilution overhang from existing equity awards. Q1 2026 buyback bought back 1.2M shares while vesting/granting net ~700K — buyback is net retiring shares but pace is barely faster than dilution.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: SBC at 13.8% of revenue is high but not abnormal for sub-scale SaaS. The economic story: ~$95M of annual SBC is being neutralized by ~$280M of buybacks (FY25+Q1'26) — so net share count is declining, but the cash cost of running that program is large relative to free cash flow ($170M OCF). If buybacks slow, dilution would re-emerge. Honest disclosure but a structural drag on per-share value.

supplemental_signals.insider_purchases_buyer: David J. Henshall (independent director, joined board 2025-04-02)

summary: BL is a -50.9% drawdown SaaS name where the Form-4 tape REJECTS any management-conviction narrative: in 12 months across 109 Form-4 filings, ONE open-market purchase ($486K by new director Henshall, Aug 2025 @ $48.60, who himself did not add at $30) vs $5.97M of officer/director SALES (P:S = 0.08x). CEO Owen Ryan, co-CEO/founder Tucker, and CFO Villanova have ZERO personal open-market activity (buys or sells) — pure RSU recipients with no risk-taking. Director Hughes sold $49K just 4 days before cutoff (T-4) — selling INTO weakness. Parallel to this, two activists circle: Engaged Capital launched a January 2026 proxy contest alleging Board 'rejected a credible acquisition offer' and got two board seats via cooperation agreement; Fivespan Partners filed 5.1% 13D in March. At the May 7 AGM, 38% voted AGAINST say-on-pay and a board-declassification proposal passed 99.6%. Operationally: three restructuring rounds in 9 months (230 positions cut, ~12% of workforce), customer count declining for 5 straight quarters (-3.5% net), GAAP net income down 85% (partly tax-driven optical). The 2026 convertible was paid off cleanly in March, so balance sheet is not the issue. M&A is the only positive optionality but the precedent (rejected offer) cuts against it materializing soon. Severity: 1 PASS / 5 MODERATE / 2 SEVERE / 1 RED_FLAG / 0 UNVERIFIABLE. Verdict: SHORT-tier — the insider-vs-narrative test fails decisively and operational deterioration (three restructurings + customer churn) is on a structural rather than cyclical path.
